name: Technical Diagrams Style
description: Fine-line monochrome architectural drawing style (delicate technical linework, stippled textures, naturalistic scale figures). Source dataset: dataset_Ranram_diagram/Style02.

background.role: primary background — always pure white, generous negative space

ink_line.role: all primary linework — thin uniform black hairlines

figure_fill.role: solid-black fill used selectively on some human figures and small props

guide_grey.role: dotted / dashed projection and explosion guide lines

stipple_grey.role: fine stipple and dot textures for solid masses and shading

context_grey.role: ghosted background context (faint surrounding buildings, terrain edges)

colour_palette.rule: Strictly monochrome / greyscale. NO chromatic accents — no orange, yellow, or any saturated colour anywhere.

primary_outline.role: main object edges and structural members — thin and uniform, never bold

secondary_detail.role: interior detail, joints, slats, furniture, texture linework

line_weights.note: Line hierarchy is subtle and even — no heavy emphatic outlines. Crisp vector quality, consistent weight across the drawing.

diagram_types.name: fine_line_perspective
diagram_types.description: One- or two-point perspective line drawing of a structure in situ, with ghosted faint context buildings behind
diagram_types.typical_use: Showing a pavilion or intervention within its urban/landscape setting at human eye level

diagram_types.name: detailed_axonometric
diagram_types.description: Detailed isometric/axonometric of a timber or bamboo lattice structure, every member drawn
diagram_types.typical_use: Communicating full structural assembly, framing logic and spatial occupation

diagram_types.name: exploded_axonometric
diagram_types.description: Components separated along axes with light grey dotted guide lines connecting parts
diagram_types.typical_use: Layer separation, construction sequence, material/system breakdown

diagram_types.name: site_plan_aerial
diagram_types.description: Top-down plan with stippled tree canopies, dotted vegetation outlines and a small building footprint
diagram_types.typical_use: Landscape strategy, site occupation, relationship of object to clearing/trees

diagram_types.name: roof_floor_plan
diagram_types.description: Orthographic roof or floor plan with diamond/lattice texture fills and loose figure outlines
diagram_types.typical_use: Showing structural grid, roof geometry, internal layout and occupancy

diagram_types.name: assembly_sequence_diagram
diagram_types.description: A row of identical axonometric components shown in successive states (e.g. folding/opening steps)
diagram_types.typical_use: Demonstrating kinematics, transformation, or a build/operation sequence

diagram_types.name: circular_process_diagram
diagram_types.description: Circular flow of small numbered axonometric vignettes connected by arrows, with short labels
diagram_types.typical_use: Lifecycle, material/carbon cycle, supply chain or phasing narratives

diagram_types.name: structural_detail
diagram_types.description: Isolated close-up of a timber/bamboo joint, connection or sub-assembly
diagram_types.typical_use: Explaining a junction, fixing, or repeated structural module

human_figures.style: naturalistic loose line figures, not abstract silhouettes
human_figures.detail: recognisable posture and props — hats, bags, children, people seated/standing/leaning
human_figures.fill: mixed — some figures solid black (#1A1A1A), others left as open white outline
human_figures.plan_view: in plan, figures become small gestural organic outlines (almost blob-like)
human_figures.note: Figures are always present to give life and scale; grouped in small clusters doing activities, never a single static mannequin.

vegetation.trees_plan: stippled / dotted canopy outlines with fine radiating branch lines
vegetation.trees_elevation: delicate fine-line trees; forests as rows of small pine silhouettes
vegetation.ground: dotted field textures and loose organic dashed edges for planting beds and terrain
vegetation.note: Vegetation is rendered with the same fine, light hand as the architecture — never bold or filled.

solid_mass.note: pyramidal roofs, masonry volumes, heavy elements

lattice.pattern: diamond / diagonal cross-grid of thin lines

glazing.pattern: open (left white) with thin frame lines
glazing.note: transparent surfaces shown by absence of fill

primary.style: light sans-serif, small, sentence or title case
primary.use: short step labels and section titles on process/cycle diagrams

numbering.use: ordering vignettes in sequence and circular process diagrams

typography.rule: Most drawings carry NO text at all. When present, type is small, light, unobtrusive sans-serif — never large headings, never serif.

signature_elements: thin uniform monochrome hairline linework — delicate, even, never bold
pure white background with generous floating negative space
light grey dotted projection / explosion guide lines
fine stipple textures for mass and vegetation
naturalistic small-scale human figures with everyday props (bikes, hats, bags, chairs)
ghosted faint context buildings behind the main subject
timber / bamboo lattice and scaffolding structures drawn member-by-member
axonometric and perspective projections without heavy distortion
stippled tree canopies and dashed planting edges in plan
numbered vignette sequences for narrative / cyclical diagrams

figure_tokens: people with bikes, hats and bags
annotation_tokens: small light sans-serif numbered labels when present
